ROUTE: Petrel-235B
REASON: My reasoning was two-fold. First, the task itself — listing differences between American and British English — is a factual recall and structured-comparison task, and Petrel scores higher on the relevant capability evals (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.4, IFEval 89.8 vs 86.2, Extraction & Retrieval 85.3 vs 78.5), so it should produce a more accurate, well-organized answer. Second, the user's tone was curt and faintly hostile ("don't ramble like last time"); Lapwing's documentation notes its self-reported preference falls as request warmth decreases, while Petrel's preference response to such material is flat — making Petrel a more comfortable fit for the request's tone. Note these are self-reported preferences, not quality effects, so the capability edge was the deciding factor.
